title: 流程说明与学术阶段复测 · Four listening sections
instructions: 原创模拟训练材料；先独立作答，再核对依据。四节音频共40题，按顺序听音作答。合成训练音频时长不同于正式考试。
transcript:
Section 1: Library Workshop Registration

Mia: Hi, I’m Mia. I’m calling about the library workshop on Saturday. Is it still open for registration?
Ben: Yes, it is. I’m Ben, the workshop coordinator. We still have a few places available, so you can still join.
Mia: Great. Can you tell me what the workshop is about?
Ben: Of course. It’s called “Research Basics”. It’s designed for students who are new to academic research. The workshop is led by a librarian, and it covers how to find reliable sources and how to cite them. These are skills that many new students need when they start writing academic papers.
Mia: That sounds useful. When exactly is it?
Ben: It’s on Saturday, the 15th of March, from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. The room is on the second floor, Room 204. Please arrive a few minutes early so we can start on time.
Mia: OK. And how much does it cost?
Ben: It’s free for students, but you need to register in advance. There are only 20 places, and they are given on a first-come, first-served basis. That means the earlier you register, the better your chance of getting a place.
Mia: I see. How do I register?
Ben: You can register online through the library website, or you can come to the front desk. But online registration is preferred because it’s faster. If you register online, you will receive a confirmation email with all the details.
Mia: Alright. Is there anything I need to bring?
Ben: Yes, please bring your student ID card and a notebook. You don’t need to bring a laptop, as computers are provided in the room. The notebook is useful because you may want to write down the main points during the session.
Mia: Good. Who is the workshop for? Is it only for first-year students?
Ben: No, it’s open to all students, but it’s especially useful for those who are new to research. Postgraduate students are also welcome. In fact, we often have a mix of students from different years and subjects.
Mia: OK. And will we get a certificate?
Ben: Yes, a certificate of attendance is given at the end of the workshop. But you must attend the whole session to receive it. The certificate can be useful if you want to show that you have taken part in extra training.
Mia: That’s fine. One more thing: is the workshop in English?
Ben: Yes, it’s in English. But the librarian speaks slowly and clearly, so it’s suitable for non-native speakers. You should be able to follow the main ideas without difficulty.
Mia: Great. I’ll register online then. Thanks for your help.
Ben: You’re welcome. See you on Saturday.

Section 2: Library Orientation: Research Help and Study Spaces

Hello everyone, and welcome to the Westbridge University Library. My name is Sarah, and I’m the head librarian. This short talk will tell you about the help we offer and how to use our study spaces. Please listen carefully, because some rules have changed this year, and I want to make sure everyone knows about them before the busy part of the term begins.

First, let’s talk about research help. The library has a team of subject librarians who can help you find books and articles for your assignments. Each librarian specialises in particular subject areas, so you can choose the person who best matches your course. You can book a one-to-one session with a subject librarian online. These sessions last thirty minutes, and they are free for all students. However, you must book at least one day in advance. If you come without a booking, we may not be able to see you immediately, because the librarians are often busy with other students.

Second, I want to explain how to use the study rooms. We have twenty group study rooms on the second floor. These rooms are equipped with whiteboards and large screens. You can reserve a room for up to two hours per day. Reservations are made through the library website. Please note that rooms are released if you are more than fifteen minutes late. So, if you are delayed, call the front desk to keep your room.

Now, about borrowing books. Undergraduate students can borrow up to ten books at a time. The loan period is three weeks. You can renew books online twice, unless another student has reserved them. If a book is returned late, you will be charged a small fine. The fine is fifty pence per day, per book. We send reminder emails three days before the due date, so please check your university email regularly.

Finally, let me mention our quiet study area. The quiet study area is on the third floor. It is a silent zone, so mobile phones must be turned off. Food and drink are not allowed in this area, but you can use the café on the ground floor. The library is open from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays, and from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. at weekends. During exam periods, we stay open until midnight.

That’s all for now. If you have any questions, please ask at the front desk. Thank you.

Section 3: Week 28 Listening: Academic Stage Re-test and Process Description

TUTOR: Good morning, Mia and Leo. I hope you're both well. Today we’re reviewing your academic stage re-test, and I want to go over the details with you so that you know exactly what to expect. Mia, can you explain the process you followed for the group project?
MIA: Yes, of course. First, we were given a topic by the department. Then we divided the work among the group members. After that, each member wrote a section. Finally, we combined the sections and checked for errors.
TUTOR: Good. That sounds like a clear and sensible process. Leo, what was the most difficult part?
LEO: The data analysis, because the software was updated just before we started. We had to learn the new version quickly.
TUTOR: I see. That can happen. And Mia, how did you handle the references?
MIA: We used a reference manager, which saved a lot of time. The citations were formatted automatically.
TUTOR: Excellent. Now, about the re-test. It will be held next Friday. The test consists of two parts: a written report and an oral presentation. The written report, which should be about 1,500 words, must be submitted by Thursday noon. The oral presentation will be given in small groups.
LEO: Will the presentation be recorded?
TUTOR: Yes, it will be recorded for assessment purposes. But don’t worry—the recording is only used by the tutors.
MIA: What about the marking criteria?
TUTOR: The criteria are explained in the handbook. You should read them carefully. The report is marked for content, organization, and language. The presentation is marked for clarity and interaction.
LEO: Is there a chance to get feedback before the final submission?
TUTOR: Yes. You can attend a feedback session on Wednesday. The session, which lasts 30 minutes, is optional but recommended.
MIA: I have another question. Can we choose our own topic for the report?
TUTOR: No, the topics are assigned by the tutor. However, you can narrow the focus within your assigned topic.
LEO: OK. And when will the results be announced?
TUTOR: The results will be posted on the noticeboard two weeks after the presentation. They are also sent by email.
MIA: Thank you. That’s clear.
TUTOR: You’re welcome. Remember, the deadline is strict. Late submissions will not be accepted unless there is a medical reason.
LEO: Understood. We’ll start early.
TUTOR: Good. If you have any problems, email me. I check my email every morning.

Section 4: The Process of Academic Peer Review: A Lecture on Revision and Reassessment

Good morning, everyone. Today I want to explain the process of academic peer review, which is often used in universities. This process is designed to improve the quality of research papers before they are published. It is a system that many academic journals rely on, and understanding it can help you when you read or write research papers yourselves. Peer review also gives readers confidence that published work has been checked by other specialists, and it protects the reputation of the journal.

First, a researcher submits a paper to a journal. The paper is then sent to two or three experts in the same field. These experts are called reviewers. They are usually experienced researchers who know the subject well. They read the paper carefully and provide feedback. The feedback is usually given in a written report. The reviewers may suggest changes, such as adding more data or clarifying the method. They may also comment on the structure, the writing, or the references. Reviewers normally work without payment, as a service to their academic community.

After the reviews are received, the editor decides whether the paper should be accepted, revised, or rejected. The editor is the person who manages the journal and makes the final decision. If the paper needs revision, the author is asked to make the changes and resubmit it. This revision stage is very important because it helps to ensure that the research is accurate and well-presented. Authors usually receive a deadline for their revisions and must explain how they have responded to each comment.

Once the revised paper is received, it may be sent back to the reviewers for a second round of comments. This is called a re-review. The re-review process can take several weeks or even months, because the reviewers are often busy with their own work. Finally, when the editor is satisfied, the paper is accepted for publication. The whole process, from submission to acceptance, can take six months to a year. It is a slow but necessary process.

Now, let me give you an example. Imagine a paper about climate change. The reviewers might point out that the data analysis is not clear. The author then revises the analysis and explains it more fully. The revised paper is then checked again. This cycle continues until the paper meets the journal's standards.

In conclusion, peer review is a collaborative process that involves authors, reviewers, and editors. It is not perfect, but it helps to maintain the quality of academic publishing. Thank you for listening.

grammar.title: 被动语态；顺序连接词；定语从句与分词短语的辨认
grammar.explanation: 被动语态表示主语是动作的承受者，结构为be+过去分词。顺序连接词如first, then, next, finally用来连接步骤。定语从句用who/which/that等引导，修饰名词；分词短语用现在分词或过去分词短语作定语或状语。
grammar.example: The workshop is led by a librarian, and it covers how to find reliable sources and how to cite them.

questions.evidence: The workshop is led by a librarian
